title: Speaking practice: Evidence, Data, and Directions
description: Eight speaking tasks. Students check an addition, explain a crossing guard's job, argue from seed data, give directions to a substitute, present a class vote, pick a read-aloud book, explain shadows, and explain a late assignment. Students record two takes; teachers or students review the recordings.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: Ana and Ben both solved 25 + 38. They got different answers.
Ana says the answer is 53.
Ben says the answer is 63. Here are Ben's steps: 25 + 30 = 55. Then 55 + 8 = 63.
You are their math partner. Tell them who is correct and how you know.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: Imagine this scene near a school. A crossing guard in a bright yellow vest stands in the street. She holds up a red stop sign. Cars are stopped on both sides of the street. A group of children walks across the street in the crosswalk.
Your younger cousin asks, “Why is that person standing in the street?” Explain how the crossing guard keeps the children safe.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: Two students tested what seeds need to sprout. Each student put 6 radish seeds on a paper towel inside a plastic bag. Both bags stayed in the same warm place for 5 days.
Bag A: the paper towel was wet. After 5 days, 5 of the 6 seeds had sprouted.
Bag B: the paper towel was dry. After 5 days, 0 of the 6 seeds had sprouted.
Tell your class what this test shows about what seeds need.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: Your teacher is away today. A substitute teacher, Mr. Baker, does not know the class routines. You are the classroom helper this week. Here are your notes about how to turn in homework.
1. Write your name on the paper.
2. Put the paper in the blue tray by the door.
3. Find your name on the list and make a check mark.
4. If your homework is not finished, tell the helper before lunch.
Explain the routine to Mr. Baker so he can help students follow it.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: A class voted for its favorite kind of class pet. Here are the results.
Rabbit: 5 votes
Fish: 4 votes
Hamster: 9 votes
Gecko: 7 votes
Total students who voted: 25
You will present the results to the principal. Tell which pet got the most votes, which pet got the fewest, and how many more votes the winner got than the pet in second place.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: Your class will choose one book for the teacher to read aloud next. Here are two choices.
Book A, “The Robot Who Wanted to Dance”: a funny story with short chapters. There are pictures on every page. It has 60 pages.
Book B, “Rivers of the World”: a nonfiction book with maps and photos. It has facts about five long rivers. It has 120 pages.
Speak to your classmates. Tell them which book you want and why.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: Kenji measured the length of his shadow outside three times on one sunny day. He stood in the same spot each time.
9:00 in the morning: 90 cm
12:00 noon: 20 cm
3:00 in the afternoon: 70 cm
Fact: In the morning and in the afternoon, the Sun is low in the sky. At noon, the Sun is high in the sky.
Kenji's classmate asks, “Why was my shadow so short at noon?” Explain what the data show and why the shadow changes.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: You were supposed to turn in your book report on Friday. You are turning it in on Monday. You want to explain to your teacher what happened. Here is what happened.
On Wednesday, you finished the report at home.
On Thursday night, your little brother spilled juice on the pages, so you had to write the report again.
On Friday, you had a cold and stayed home.
Tell your teacher the reasons in order. Say what you did to fix the problem. Speak politely.

items.stem: Decide whether Ana or Ben solved 25 + 38 correctly, and tell your partner how you know.

checklist: I said who is correct.
I checked Ben's steps one at a time.
I said the final answer.
I used the word because to give my reason.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: identifies Ben as correct and supports the decision by checking the steps or using another method.
Mathematical reasoning: states the intermediate sums (55, then 63) accurately.
Organization: decision first, then the check, then the final answer.
Sentence-level language: because or so clause; simple past or present tense for describing steps.

support.clue: Look at Ben's two steps. Check each step by adding. Then ask: could Ana's answer be right?
support.frame: I think ______ is correct. ______ first added ______ and got ______. Then ______ added ______ and got ______. So the answer is ______.
support.model: Mentor example. About different numbers: “Eli says 47 + 26 = 63. Rosa says 47 + 26 = 73. Rosa added 47 + 20 = 67 and then 67 + 6 = 73. I agree with Rosa because both of her steps are correct. Eli forgot to carry the extra ten from 7 + 6 = 13.” Now decide about Ana and Ben.

items.stem: Explain to your cousin how the crossing guard keeps the children safe and what the drivers do.

checklist: I told what the crossing guard does.
I told how the children stay safe.
I told what the drivers do.
I used because or so.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: explains the guard’s role and at least one effect on the children or the drivers.
Cause and effect: connects the guard's action (stopping cars) to the result (children cross safely).
Vocabulary: crossing guard, crosswalk, traffic, safe, and stop used accurately.
Sentence-level language: because or so to link cause and effect.

support.clue: Look at what the crossing guard holds and what the cars do. Then look at what the children are doing.
support.frame: The crossing guard ______. When the cars ______, the children can ______. This helps because ______.
support.model: Mentor example. About a lifeguard: “The lifeguard watches the swimmers from a tall chair. When a swimmer needs help, the lifeguard jumps in the water. This helps because swimmers stay safe.” Now explain how the crossing guard helps.

facts: Crossing guards stop traffic so that people can cross a street safely.

items.stem: Use the results to make a claim about what radish seeds need in order to sprout, and support it with evidence.

checklist: I made a claim about what seeds need.
I used numbers from both bags as evidence.
I said what was the same in both bags and what was different.
I used because or this shows that.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: claims that seeds need water to sprout and supports it with data from both bags.
Evidence: cites 5 of 6 and 0 of 6 and connects the numbers to wet and dry paper towels.
Scientific reasoning: notes that the warm place, time, and seed type were the same, so water is the likely reason.
Sentence-level language: comparison and claim-evidence connectors (however, this shows that, because).
Vocabulary: sprout, seeds, wet, dry, and test accurate.

support.clue: Compare the two bags. What was different? What was the same? Use the numbers to show the result.
support.frame: My claim is that seeds need ______ to sprout. In Bag A, ______ of the ______ seeds sprouted. In Bag B, ______. This shows that ______ because ______.
support.model: Mentor example. About ice: “My claim is that salt water freezes more slowly than fresh water. In Cup A with fresh water, the water was frozen after 3 hours. In Cup B with salty water, the water was still liquid after 3 hours. This shows that salt makes freezing slower because both cups were in the same freezer.” Now make your claim about radish seeds.

facts: Seeds need water to begin to sprout (germinate).
In the test, 5 of 6 seeds sprouted in the wet towel and 0 of 6 in the dry towel.

items.stem: Tell the substitute teacher, Mr. Baker, the steps for turning in homework in your class.

checklist: I told all four steps in order.
I used command words or must/should (write, put, find).
I used sequence words such as first, next, then, and last.
I spoke politely to Mr. Baker.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: gives all four steps accurately and in order, including the rule about unfinished homework.
Organization: sequence words (first, next, then, last) and a clear beginning and end.
Sentence-level language: imperative or modal forms (students write, they should put) used consistently.
Vocabulary: tray, list, check mark, and helper used accurately.

support.clue: Read the numbered steps. Decide what each student does first, next, and last. Think about what to say about the unfinished homework.
support.frame: First, students ______. Next, they ______. Then, they ______. If homework is not finished, they ______.
support.model: Mentor example. About lining up for lunch: “First, students put their books away. Next, they stand behind the line leader. Then, they walk quietly to the lunchroom. If a student forgets a lunch card, he or she tells the teacher.” Now explain the homework routine to Mr. Baker.

items.stem: Present the results of the class pet vote to the principal in a short talk.

checklist: I said which pet got the most votes and how many.
I said which pet got the fewest votes and how many.
I said how many more votes the winner got than the pet in second place.
I used words like most, fewest, total, and more than.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: reports hamster with the most (9) and fish with the fewest (4) and finds the difference of 2 votes between hamster and gecko.
Data accuracy: all numbers match the list; the total of 25 is stated correctly if included.
Organization: most, then fewest, then the comparison, then the total.
Vocabulary: votes, most, fewest, total, and more than used accurately.
Sentence-level language: comparison structures (got more votes than, the most votes of all).

support.clue: Scan the numbers and find the biggest and the smallest. Then find the second biggest. Decide how to compare the biggest with the second.
support.frame: The class voted for ______ pets. ______ got the most votes with ______. ______ got the fewest votes with ______. ______ got ______ more votes than ______. In all, ______ students voted.
support.model: Mentor example. About a field trip vote: “The class voted on where to go. The zoo got 11 votes, the museum got 7 votes, and the park got 2 votes. The zoo got the most votes. The park got the fewest votes. The zoo got 4 more votes than the museum. In all, 20 students voted.” Now present the pet vote.

facts: Hamster has the most votes (9) and fish the fewest (4).
9 − 7 = 2, so hamster has 2 more votes than gecko.

items.stem: Choose Book A or Book B for your class read-aloud and give reasons from the descriptions.

checklist: I chose Book A or Book B.
I gave two reasons that use details from the descriptions.
I used because or since.
I spoke to my classmates in a friendly, clear way.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: chooses one book and supports the choice with two reasons from the descriptions.
Evidence: uses details from the prompt (short chapters, pictures, maps, five rivers, 60 or 120 pages).
Organization: choice, reasons, and a closing sentence that invites classmates to agree.
Sentence-level language: because, since, and also; persuasive phrases such as I think or I believe.
Vocabulary: story, nonfiction, chapters, and facts used accurately.

support.clue: Read about each book. Think about what a class would enjoy hearing out loud for several days.
support.frame: I would like to read Book ______ because ______. Also, ______. The description says ______. I hope the class chooses it because ______.
support.model: Mentor example. About a game for indoor recess: “I would like to play the card game because it is quiet. Also, anyone can learn it in two minutes. The rules say that every player gets seven cards. I hope the class chooses it because everyone can join.” Now choose a book for the read-aloud.

items.stem: Explain why Kenji's shadow changed length during the day and why it was shortest at noon.

checklist: I used the three measurements from Kenji’s notes.
I said when the shadow was the longest and the shortest.
I explained why the shadow changes using the Sun's place in the sky.
I used because or as a result.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: describes the pattern (long, short, then longer) with the measurements and gives a cause tied to the position of the Sun.
Scientific reasoning: explains that the Sun is higher in the sky at noon, so the shadow is shorter, and lower in the morning and afternoon, so the shadow is longer.
Evidence: cites 90 cm, 20 cm, and 70 cm correctly.
Sentence-level language: connectors of cause and effect and sequence (because, as a result, then).
Vocabulary: shadow, Sun, sky, length, and noon used accurately.

support.clue: Look at how the numbers change from morning to noon to afternoon. Think about where the Sun is in the sky at each time.
support.frame: At 9:00 the shadow was ______ cm, at noon it was ______ cm, and at 3:00 it was ______ cm. The shadow changes because ______. At noon the Sun is ______, so ______.
support.model: Mentor example. About a pot of water: “The water was 20 °C at the start. After five minutes it was 50 °C, and after ten minutes it was 80 °C. The temperature rose each time because the stove kept adding heat. As a result, the water got hotter and hotter.” Now explain what the shadow data show and why.

facts: A shadow is longer when the Sun is low in the sky and shorter when the Sun is high.
Around midday the Sun is highest in the sky, so shadows are shortest.
The Sun appears to move across the sky because Earth rotates.

items.stem: Explain to your teacher why your book report is late and what you did to solve the problem.

checklist: I told the reasons in order.
I used because, so, or as a result.
I told what I did to fix the problem.
I spoke politely to my teacher.
exemplar: Task fulfilment: explains the late report with the sequence of reasons (finished, spilled, rewrote, absent) and says how the problem was handled.
Organization: events in time order with a clear opening apology or greeting and a closing statement.
Sentence-level language: cause-and-effect connectors (because, so, as a result) and past-tense verbs with few errors.
Register: polite and respectful tone suited to a teacher.
Elaboration: includes the repair action (rewriting the report) as well as the problem.

support.clue: Put the three events in time order. Which event caused the report to be late? Which event caused you to stay home?
support.frame: I am sorry my report is late. On Wednesday, ______. On Thursday night, ______, so ______. Then on Friday, ______. As a result, ______. To fix the problem, I ______.
support.model: Mentor example. About a missing permission slip: “I am sorry I do not have my permission slip. On Monday, my aunt signed it. On Tuesday, the rain soaked my backpack, so the paper got ruined. As a result, I asked my aunt to sign a new one. I will bring it tomorrow.” Now explain why your book report is late.
